title: How languages change
examples: Teacher, why is the word 'awesome' so new?
Can you give me an example of a word that changed its meaning?
What is the difference between slang and dialect?

explain.say: Language changes all the time over many years.
Old English words are very different from words we use now.
People often borrow words from other languages we meet.
Slang words are very informal and used by certain groups.
A real-life example is when we use 'awesome' for something great.
A common mistake is thinking all new words are slang.

items: New words are not always slang

draw.text: Mistake: Assuming all new words are slang

faq.q: Why does English have so many borrowed words?
faq.a: English has borrowed words because it has been in contact with many different cultures. People naturally adopt useful words from languages they interact with.
asks: Where did English get so many words from?
Is it normal for a language to borrow words?

faq.q: How do we know if a word is slang?
faq.a: Slang words change very quickly and are usually used in very informal settings. If you see it in a textbook, it is probably not slang.
asks: What is the difference between slang and dialect?

faq.a: No, language change can happen very quickly, especially with slang. Sometimes a word can become popular overnight.
asks: How fast can a word change meaning?

faq.q: What is the difference between a dialect and slang?
faq.a: A dialect is a form of language spoken by a specific group of people in a region. Slang is more about current, informal usage within a group.
asks: Is a regional accent the same as a dialect?
Does slang mean the same thing everywhere?

faq.q: Are there any words that never change?
faq.a: No language is completely static; all languages are always evolving. Even common words can gain new meanings over time.
asks: Does any word stay the same forever?

facts: Old English was heavily influenced by Germanic languages.
Borrowing words happens when cultures interact through trade or conquest.
Slang vocabulary is often temporary and highly localized.
Language change can affect pronunciation, grammar, and vocabulary.

quiz.say: The word 'kindergarten' is an example of:
quiz.why: The word 'kindergarten' comes directly from German, showing borrowing from another language.

wrong.0: Slang words are informal and temporary; 'kindergarten' is a fixed, formal term.
wrong.1: It is not an original modern English word, but an adopted one.
wrong.3: Old English words usually relate to early Germanic roots, not modern German terms.

quiz.say: If a word changes its meaning over centuries, this is called:
quiz.why: Semantic shift describes the change in the meaning of a word over time, like 'nice' once meaning foolish.

wrong.1: This refers to changes in sentence structure, not the meaning of a single word.
wrong.2: Language shift refers to an entire community adopting a new language, not just one word's meaning.
wrong.3: Borrowing means taking a word from another language, not changing its original meaning.

quiz.say: Which of these words is most likely to be temporary slang?
quiz.why: Slang terms like 'drip' change very rapidly and are tied to current youth culture.

wrong.0: Basic elements rarely undergo rapid, superficial changes in common usage.
wrong.2: This word has been in use for a very long time with a stable meaning.
wrong.3: This is a core vocabulary word with deep historical roots.
